info.title: uptime-monitor — read-only API
info.summary: The reachability history the page shows, as JSON
info.description: Read-only and unauthenticated, served on the socket the page already binds: it never writes and it never needs a credential. Every success is an object whose `data` holds an array and whose `meta` echoes the request; every failure is an object with a stable `code` and a fixed `message`. The data routes stream: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no `Content-Length`, gzip on the fly when the client accepts it. A breaking change means a new `/api/vN` prefix.

get.summary: Faults, down time, and up runs per UTC day, oldest first
get.description: The window is the last 30 days when the request names none, and it may be as wide as the accepted domain allows (47 482 days at most): only the days the page returns are read, so the cost follows `limit`, not the span. A day that the window clips at its edges counts only what falls inside it; a day that has not begun yet states no faults, no down time and no up run, because unelapsed time is not measured; and the UTC day still running is flagged `partial`: its average and longest up run cover the last 24 hours, like the detail page.

get.summary: One target's state on a regular grid, oldest first
get.description: Samples one target's timeline every `step` seconds. A sample states the state that held at its instant, `up`, `degraded`, `down` or `unknown` as `v`, next to `t` in epoch milliseconds; when the request asks with `ts` or `ts=true` it also states `ts`, localised in `tz`. An instant after `now` is `unknown` because unelapsed time is not measured. Samples lie on the epoch grid of `step`: `from <= at < to` and `at` is a multiple of `step * 1000`. The window is the last hour when the request names no `from`, and `to` defaults to `now`. `target` is required. `limit` and `offset` count samples, and only the timeline the page needs is read, so the cost follows `limit`, not the width of the window.

get.summary: One target's state as JSON Lines, the meta first
get.description: The same page as `/api/v1/timeseries`, written as JSON Lines (`application/x-ndjson`): the first line is `{"meta": {...}}`, then every following line is one sample object `{"t": ..., "v": ...}`, each terminated by a newline. No array is opened, so a client consumes a record as soon as its line arrives. The parameters, the grid, the paging, and the errors are those of `/api/v1/timeseries`; a refusal before the first line is the usual JSON error object with the HTTP status, and a failure after it closes the stream and stays in the log.

200.description: The meta object on the first line, then one sample per line

schema.description: One JSON object per line: `{"meta": {...}}` first, then `{"t": <epoch ms>, "v": <state>}` records

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API

Target.name: target
Target.description: Canonical key (`icmp://1.1.1.1`) or the label of a target. An unknown value answers `404 UNKNOWN_TARGET`.

TargetRequired.name: target
TargetRequired.description: Canonical key (`icmp://1.1.1.1`) or the label of a target; required on this route. An unknown value answers `404 UNKNOWN_TARGET` and a missing one answers `400 INVALID_PARAMETER`.

From.name: from
From.description: Start of the window, inclusive. Accepted forms: `now`; a relative instant such as `-1h`, `-2d`, `-1mo` or `-1y` (`s`, `m`, `h` are exact, `d`, `w`, `mo`, `y` step the calendar in `tz`); epoch milliseconds; `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` with an optional `.fff` fraction and an optional `Z` or `±HH:MM` suffix. A value without a suffix is read in `tz`, or in UTC when `tz` is absent. An instant lies between `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` and `2100-01-01T00:00:00Z`, both accepted; a value outside answers `400 INVALID_PARAMETER`.

To.name: to
To.description: End of the window, exclusive, in the same forms and inside the same calendar domain as `from`. It must be later than `from`, and it may be in the future, so a whole month or year can be asked for; an instant after `now` states no measured state.

Tz.name: tz
Tz.description: The zone a `from` or `to` value without an explicit offset is read in: `UTC`, a fixed offset such as `+02:00`, or an IANA name such as `Europe/Rome`. Defaults to UTC. A value with its own `Z` or offset ignores `tz`. The meta echoes the spelling the request used. An unknown zone answers `400 INVALID_PARAMETER`.

Ts.name: ts
Ts.description: When present (bare or `ts=true`), every sample also states `ts`, the instant rendered in RFC 3339 and localised in `tz`; `ts=false` keeps only the numeric `t`. An absent parameter states no `ts`.

Step.name: step
Step.description: The grid of the timeseries: a number of seconds between 1 and 86400, or a duration such as `30s`, `2m`, `1h`, or `1d`. Every sample sits on an epoch multiple of it.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: How many records the page holds.

LimitWide.name: limit
LimitWide.description: How many samples the page holds. The answer is streamed, one record per chunk, so a wide page does not build the document in memory.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: How many records to skip. Paging a list that grows at the top can repeat a record; use `from`/`to` for a stable window.

BadRequest.description: A parameter the route does not accept, a value out of range, or a window that ends before it starts

UnknownTarget.description: The `target` filter names no target in the database

Unavailable.description: The database is missing or was never opened by this tool

Sample.description: The state of the answer's target at one grid instant. The target is stated once in `meta.filters.target` and is not repeated in every record.

t.description: The grid instant in epoch milliseconds

ts.description: The same instant as `t` rendered in RFC 3339, localised in `tz`; present only when the request asks for it with `ts` or `ts=true`

v.description: The state that held at the instant; unknown before the first event and after now

step.description: The grid of the timeseries in seconds; present on that route only

total.description: How many records match the filters, whatever the page holds

target.description: The canonical key the filter resolved to, or null

from.description: The start actually applied, defaults included

to.description: The end actually applied, defaults included

tz.description: The zone the request named, as it spelled it; absent when it named none, which reads as UTC

target.description: The canonical key of the target

label.description: The label of the target, or null

interface.description: The interface the probe is bound to, or null for the default route

stateSinceMs.description: The same instant in epoch milliseconds

lastRttUs.description: The round-trip time of the last successful probe, in microseconds

upForMs.description: How long the target has been up without a drop; null while it is not up

Fault.description: One fault: the `down` transition that opened it, its cause, and the return that closed it. A fault always opens on a `down` event, so no `state` and no round-trip time are stated: both would be constants.

cause.description: The code of the failure, such as ICMP.NO_REPLY

causeMessage.description: The standard message of that cause, as it was rendered

endedAt.description: The instant the target came back; null while it is still down

durationMs.description: How long the fault lasted; null while it is still open

ongoing.description: True while the target is still down

target.description: The canonical key of the target when the request filters by one; null when the record aggregates every target

faults.description: Faults that started inside the day and the window

downMs.description: Time spent down inside the day, clipped to the window

avgUpRunMs.description: Mean of the up runs inside the day; null when the day holds none

longestUpRunMs.description: The longest up run inside the day

partial.description: True for the UTC day still running: its runs cover the last 24 hours

status.description: The HTTP status of the answer

parameter.description: The query parameter the answer is about, when there is one
